Introduction

What Is an IEC?

An Import Export Code is a 10-digit identifier issued by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), mandatory for any business or individual looking to import goods into India or export goods out of it. Without an IEC, customs clearance for import or export shipments simply cannot happen.

The code is PAN-based, issued once, and doesn't require periodic renewal, though updating your IEC details annually is required to keep it active.

Why It Matters

What an IEC Enables

🚢

Legal Import & Export

Mandatory identifier for customs clearance on any cross-border shipment, in either direction.

🏦

International Payments

Required by banks to process inward and outward remittances tied to import-export transactions.

🎁

Export Scheme Benefits

Access to government export incentive and benefit schemes that require a valid IEC.

🔁

No Renewal Needed

Issued once and valid for the business's lifetime, subject to annual online updating.

Eligibility

Who Needs an IEC

  • Any business or individual planning to import goods into India
  • Any business or individual planning to export goods out of India
  • Applicable to Proprietorships, Partnerships, LLPs and Companies alike
  • A valid PAN and business bank account are prerequisites

Step-by-Step

Registration Process & Timeline

1. Document Collection

We gather your PAN, address proof and bank details for the application.

2. Online Application

The application is filed on the DGFT portal along with the applicable fee.

3. IEC Issuance

Once processed, the IEC is issued digitally — typically within a few working days, though timelines can vary.

Required Documents

What You'll Need

  • PAN of the business entity or individual
  • Proof of business address
  • Bank account details with a cancelled cheque
  • Digital photograph of the applicant (for individuals/proprietors)
